solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Island nearly close after drama backtracking

indicators.note: to backtrack is to go back the way you came, so the word for drama is read from its end
nearly means not quite all, so the word for close loses its final letter
after says the trimmed word for close goes second, behind the drama word

blocks.note: Noh is classical Japanese masked drama
to close a door is to shut it

explanation.surface: Someone is about to wrap up a trip to an island once they have finished revisiting a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Noh is Japanese masked theatre and the answer is a Japanese island.
explanation.definitionFit: Honshu is the largest of the main islands of Japan, home to Tokyo.

clue.text: Female’s accepting lead on family film, new actress

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word for female holds the next letters inside it

blocks.note: her is the female pronoun; the 's reads as 'is'
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
U is the British film certificate for universal, family viewing
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A woman is signing up for a new family film role as its leading lady.
explanation.walkthrough: HER takes in PB on U to give HEPBUR, then N. 'Lead' looks like a starring role, but it is the metal; U is the British certificate for films suitable for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Audrey and Katharine Hepburn were both celebrated Hollywood film stars, so the surname names an actress.

clue.text: Writer’s point about Old English figure of myth

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the writer's point wraps around the next letter

blocks.note: the nib is the writing point of a pen
O is a standard abbreviation for old
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An author makes a point about Old English and a figure from mythology.
explanation.walkthrough: NIB goes around O, then E follows. 'Old English' looks like one phrase, the language, but it splits into two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Niobe boasted of her children, lost them all, and was turned to weeping stone.

clue.text: Dope, one tucking into hot kebab

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so the letter for one sits within the other letters

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
a shish is a kebab, as in shish kebab
a means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: Someone high on drugs is wolfing down a spicy kebab.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes between H and SHISH. 'Tucking into' reads as eating, which suits the food, but it signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for cannabis, and hashish is the resin form of that drug.

clue.text: Free tag and cut stringy material

indicators.note: letters set free are loosened from their order and can be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for a shop: remove the price label and trim some string.
explanation.definitionFit: Catgut is a tough cord made from animal intestine, used for instrument strings and sutures.

clue.text: Plug fissure undirected

blocks.note: to plug a product is to advertise it, and an ad is an advert
a rift is a crack or fissure

explanation.surface: Someone tries to fill a crack in the ground without any plan or guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' looks like a stopper for the fissure, but it is a piece of publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adrift floats with no steering or course, so it is without direction.

clue.text: Emu got ill, sickly bird

indicators.note: something sickly is in poor shape, so these letters are put into a different form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A zoo report: the emu has fallen sick and is looking poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hands over one bird, the emu, as a distraction; the bird wanted is a different one made from its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The guillemot is a black-and-white seabird of the auk family that nests on cliff ledges.

clue.text: Elderly being squeezed by tax is disaster

indicators.note: something squeezed by another is pressed inside it, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: to tax someone's patience is to try it
aged means elderly

explanation.surface: Pensioners being financially squeezed by taxation is a calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax' reads as a levy, but here it is the verb meaning to strain, as in taxing someone's patience.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a terrible event causing great suffering, which is what a disaster is.

clue.text: Spiv from Kentish Town in Queens needing revolver beforehand

indicators.note: in places the Kentish town inside the pair of royal letters
beforehand says the revolver comes first, ahead of everything else

blocks.note: a wheel is something that revolves
ER (Elizabeth Regina) is a queen; two queens give two of them
Deal is a seaside town in Kent

explanation.surface: A shady character from the London district of Kentish Town, in the New York borough of Queens, needs a gun first.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentish Town and Queens look like London and New York places, and a revolver looks like a pistol; all three are split differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiv is a British word for a flashy small-time dodgy trader, which is what a wheeler-dealer is.

clue.text: Partner, East or West

blocks.note: first meaning: informal British word for a colleague or companion
second meaning: at the bridge table each of these players is the other's opposite number

explanation.walkthrough: Bridge pairs North with South and East with West, so East's partner sits opposite. The four letters also read the same from east or west.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is British slang, short for opposite number, for a mate or counterpart.

clue.text: Drunk lad is pro, he gets round

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about out of line, so the letters that follow are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boozy young man who turned professional ends up buying a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a round of drinks at the bar, but it is the adjective for shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Spheroidal means shaped like a slightly squashed sphere, broadly round.

clue.text: Bones throbbing with rage when rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word for rage is read backwards

blocks.note: a steady throbbing sound is a hum
ire is anger or rage

explanation.surface: Someone's bones ache and pulse with fury after being turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Humeri is the plural of humerus, the long bone of the upper arm.

clue.text: Fondled nuts with ecstasy and hugged

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A night out on ecstasy ends in cuddling and caressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' sits after Fondled as if it were the thing fondled; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To enfold someone is to wrap them in your arms, so enfolded matches hugged as a past tense.

clue.text: With spades for borders, instantly weeded and prepared for bad weather

indicators.note: borders run round the outside, so the spades go on either side of the next word

blocks.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades, one for each border
to do something instantly is to do it now
to hoe a bed is to clear it of weeds

explanation.surface: A gardener edges the flower borders with a spade, weeds them quickly, and gets ready for a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: Spades and borders read as garden tools and flower beds, which suits weeded; here spades is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone snowshoed has strapped on snowshoes, ready to walk over deep snow.

clue.text: Smell something fishy when chatting

blocks.note: a whiff is a faint smell
the ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone senses a scam during a conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something fishy' reads as suspicious, but it is a literal fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To whiffle is to talk idly or trivially, so whiffling is a light form of chatting.

clue.text: Horrible memory, after being stripped of gold award

indicators.note: to be stripped of something is to lose it, so the letters for gold are taken out
something horrible is a mess, so what is left gets scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: An athlete is left with a bad memory of having a gold medal taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing OR leaves MEMY to be rearranged. Or is the heraldry word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An Emmy is the American prize for excellence in television, a famous award.

clue.text: Stones dropped? Give praise

blocks.note: first meaning: pellets of ice, hailstones, falling from the sky
second meaning: to acclaim or salute enthusiastically

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'stones dropped' is a playful description of a weather event, not rocks let fall.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is frozen precipitation in lumps, and the verb means to acclaim someone, as in hailed a hero.

clue.text: Place for waders and half of rods possessed by scientist

indicators.note: half of keeps only the first part of the word that follows
something possessed is held, so the scientist's name holds those letters

blocks.note: Joseph Henry was an American physicist; the henry, the unit of inductance, honours him
the first two of its four letters

explanation.surface: A fishing spot where anglers in waders stand with rods, half of them owned by a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: Waders sounds like anglers' boots alongside the rods, but here waders are birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A heronry is a colony where herons nest, and herons are long-legged wading birds.

clue.text: Taking care, approach nurses rather oddly

indicators.note: oddly keeps only the letters in odd-numbered positions of the word before it
to nurse is to hold close, so the word for approach cradles the selected letters

blocks.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A careful person meets nurses who are behaving a bit strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' looks like hospital staff, but it is a verb meaning holds close.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertent is a rare adjective meaning attentive or heedful, the opposite of inadvertent.

clue.text: To be around setter’s said to be a curse

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the verb is read backwards
said means spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the setter's pronoun

blocks.note: to be is to exist, or live
the setter refers to themself as I; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler is rumoured to be bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'To be' is wordplay and the second is the link. Crossword setters often call themselves 'I' or 'me'.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a malevolent glance believed to bring misfortune, a kind of curse.

clue.text: With instinct book work for boat race

blocks.note: a nose for something is an instinct for it
Job is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A rower with good instincts prepares a training plan for the Oxford and Cambridge Boat Race.
explanation.walkthrough: Boat race is Cockney rhyming slang for face. The Boat Race is the annual Oxford-Cambridge rowing contest on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose job is cosmetic surgery, work done on the face in rhyming-slang terms.

clue.text: Fabulous flyer collected by German shopkeeper

indicators.note: something collected is gathered up and held, so the abbreviation wraps round the bird

blocks.note: Ger is the abbreviation for German
the roc is a giant bird of Arabian fable

explanation.surface: A legendary bird is picked up by a German who runs a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Fabulous here means from fables, not wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer runs a shop selling food and household goods, so is a kind of shopkeeper.

clue.text: Poor farm forged invoice

indicators.note: something forged is made up or hammered into a new shape, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A struggling farm has faked its paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forged invoice' reads as fraud, but forged is the signal and invoice alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro forma is a preliminary bill sent before goods are supplied, a type of invoice.

clue.text: Out of the area, old Liverpool striker makes sudden arrival

indicators.note: out of here means without, so the letter for area is dropped

blocks.note: Ian Rush was Liverpool FC's record goalscorer in the 1980s
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A veteran footballer bursts in from outside the penalty area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The area' suggests the penalty box, apt for a striker, but it is just the letter A, removed from his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: An inrush is a sudden flooding in, of water, air or people, so a sudden arrival.

clue.text: Ammunition left by cart is narrow range

indicators.note: what is left by something is what remains after it departs, so those letters go

blocks.note: a cartridge is a round of ammunition
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bullets abandoned beside a wagon on a firing range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' suggests shooting, which goes with ammunition, but it is a range of hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow elevated crest of land, a slim line of hills.

clue.text: Homogeneous cider I sent abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean all over the place, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone exports a uniform batch of cider overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Not to be confused with indiscreet: this spelling means not separated into distinct parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indiscrete is not divided into separate parts, so uniform and homogeneous throughout.

clue.text: Combat centre party, work endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter of the word for work is lost

blocks.note: a do is a party or celebration
a job is a piece of work

explanation.surface: A military hub that keeps partying and working without a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combat centre' sounds military; it is a place for martial arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A dojo is a hall where martial arts such as judo and karate are taught and practised.

clue.text: Cultural fare, knocking back spirit in tent

indicators.note: knocking back turns something the other way, so the word for spirit runs backwards
in puts the turned word inside the tent

blocks.note: a yurt is a round felt tent of Central Asian nomads
go means energy or spirit, as in full of go

explanation.surface: Festival food: downing spirits in a marquee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back spirit' reads as drinking liquor; spirit is vigour, and it is turned round. 'Cultural' puns on the cultures that make the fare.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogurt is food made by fermenting milk with bacterial cultures, hence cultured fare.

clue.text: What can change our perception forever – bacon sandwiches

indicators.note: a sandwich holds a filling between slices, so the answer sits held within the words

blocks.note: the run of letters spans the two words

explanation.surface: A claim that bacon sandwiches will alter how we see the world for good.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is deliberately vague: the effect alters how we hear a sound, not how we see.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverb is echo added to sound, which changes how a listener perceives the space and the music.
